commit : credits _ applied target _ bucket = org : t2 : key : kx unexpected = true amount = 200 hypothesis : a race between sticky - shard mapping update and policy hot - reload causes fast - path cache entries ( priority and credit pointers ) to be re - keyed incorrectly. per - key overrides store a pointer to a tenant - scoped credit bucket ; during reassignment we are dereferencing a stale pointer and applying credits to the wrong tenant ' s bucket. enforcement uses the fast - path decision if cache present, so the wrong credits cause an allow where a deny should occur.

are you using our go sdk v0.12.1 or main?\\n\\nmaria: v0.12.1 (released), command: `go run ./cmd/sampleapp -mode=stream -token=$TOKEN`\\n\\nmaria: logs:\\n```\\n2026-03-20T14:03:12Z INFO starting generator stream\\n2026-03-20T14:03:12Z DEBUG sending client hello\\n2026-03-20T14:03:12Z DEBUG waiting for server ack\\n# network blip -> nothing received\\n# ctx cancelled by user at 14:03:17\\n2026-03-20T14:03:17Z INFO context cancelled, waiting for stream close\\n# nothing; process stuck\\n```\\n\\npriya: does the server accept an unauthenticated first frame? python sdk auto-sends an auth frame before the stream op. go sdk's generator currently expects the stream op to carry auth metadata and then waits for server to ack. if network drops at that moment we can get stuck because we never send a follow-up frame or a ping.\\n\\nalex: right \\u2014 parity note: python: send_auth_frame(); send_start(); go: send_start() with auth in metadata. if start gets lost the server has partial state and client waits.\\n\\nsam: quick workaround: wrap StartGeneratorStream in a goroutine and select on ctx.Done to close the underlying conn. but that's ugly.\\n\\nmaria: here's a tiny patch I tried locally that fixes it: set a read deadline on the stream socket and treat missing server ack as an error to abort. snippet:\\n```\\n// pseudo\\nconn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5*time.Second))\\nerr := waitForServerAck()\\nif err != nil {\\n  conn.Close()\\n  return fmt.Errorf(\\\"handshake timeout: %w\\\", err)\\n}\\n```\\n\\npriya: acceptable as interim but we should fix ergonomics in the SDK. proposal: 1) make go sdk send an explicit auth frame before Start; 2) ensure StartGeneratorStream listens to ctx.Done and closes stream proactively; 3) add small handshake timeout default (configurable).\\n\\nalex: +1. also add a sampleapp test that simulates packet loss and shows proper cancellation. this'll prevent regressions.\\n\\nmaria: opened PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4321 \\u2014 implements 2 + 3 and adds doc note. still experimenting with 1.\\n\\nci-bot: build passed for PR #4321 (linux-amd64) :white_check_mark:\\n\\nsam: can we add an explicit example in quickstarts/ generating/streaming.md showing correct context/cancel pattern? users keep tripping over this.\\n\\npriya: yes \\u2014 I'll add a short snippet: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second); defer cancel(); gen, err := client.StartGeneratorStream(ctx, opts)` and a note about network heuristics.\\n\\nalex: also file a small internal issue to audit other SDKs for handshake parity (python, js, rust). we need consistent server expectations.\\n\\nmaria: thanks all \\u2014 marking this as actionable. will follow up in PR comments with reproducible steps for the eng-oncall to run. :thumbsup:\\n\\nalex: nice find. once PR lands, let's add a tiny e2e in CI that simulates the blip.\\n\\nmaria: last note \\u2014 sampleapp onboarding doc needs to warn about cloud VPNs that pause TCP for a bit during startup. added that to the PR description.\\n\\npriya: good call.\\n\\nsam: resolving on my side after PR merge.\\n\\nmaria: thanks!\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_e0ca834bf3564579a9be2f8b820c7fdf\"\n}",

document.content:
{
  "channel": "devex",
  "thread_ts": "1785551234",
  "first_message_ts": "1785551234",
  "last_message_ts": "1785551289",
  "participants": [
    "maria",
    "alex",
    "sam",
    "priya",
    "ci-bot"
  ],
  "messages": "maria: heads up — onboarding sampleapp streaming seems to hang at the generator handshake step. repro in local with intermittent network drops.

alex: ugh, seen something similar last week. can you paste the minimal logs?

maria: pasted below. go sample app -> StartGeneratorStream(ctx) then nothing, ctx cancel doesn't close.

sam: can you share the run command? are you using our go sdk v0.12.1 or main?

maria: v0.12.1 (released), command: `go run ./cmd/sampleapp -mode=stream -token=$TOKEN`

maria: logs:
```
2026-03-20T14:03:12Z INFO starting generator stream
2026-03-20T14:03:12Z DEBUG sending client hello
2026-03-20T14:03:12Z DEBUG waiting for server ack
# network blip -> nothing received
# ctx cancelled by user at 14:03:17
2026-03-20T14:03:17Z INFO context cancelled, waiting for stream close
# nothing; process stuck
```

priya: does the server accept an unauthenticated first frame? python sdk auto-sends an auth frame before the stream op. go sdk's generator currently expects the stream op to carry auth metadata and then waits for server to ack. if network drops at that moment we can get stuck because we never send a follow-up frame or a ping.

alex: right — parity note: python: send_auth_frame(); send_start(); go: send_start() with auth in metadata. if start gets lost the server has partial state and client waits.

sam: quick workaround: wrap StartGeneratorStream in a goroutine and select on ctx.Done to close the underlying conn. but that's ugly.

maria: here's a tiny patch I tried locally that fixes it: set a read deadline on the stream socket and treat missing server ack as an error to abort. snippet:
```
// pseudo
conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5*time.Second))
err := waitForServerAck()
if err != nil {
  conn.Close()
  return fmt.Errorf("handshake timeout: %w", err)
}
```

priya: acceptable as interim but we should fix ergonomics in the SDK. proposal: 1) make go sdk send an explicit auth frame before Start; 2) ensure StartGeneratorStream listens to ctx.Done and closes stream proactively; 3) add small handshake timeout default (configurable).

alex: +1. also add a sampleapp test that simulates packet loss and shows proper cancellation. this'll prevent regressions.

maria: opened PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4321 — implements 2 + 3 and adds doc note. still experimenting with 1.

ci-bot: build passed for PR #4321 (linux-amd64) :white_check_mark:

sam: can we add an explicit example in quickstarts/ generating/streaming.md showing correct context/cancel pattern? users keep tripping over this.

priya: yes — I'll add a short snippet: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second); defer cancel(); gen, err := client.StartGeneratorStream(ctx, opts)` and a note about network heuristics.

alex: also file a small internal issue to audit other SDKs for handshake parity (python, js, rust). we need consistent server expectations.

maria: thanks all — marking this as actionable. will follow up in PR comments with reproducible steps for the eng-oncall to run. :thumbsup:

alex: nice find. once PR lands, let's add a tiny e2e in CI that simulates the blip.

maria: last note — sampleapp onboarding doc needs to warn about cloud VPNs that pause TCP for a bit during startup. added that to the PR description.

priya: good call.

sam: resolving on my side after PR merge.

maria: thanks!",

  "content_field_names": [
    "messages"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_e0ca834bf3564579a9be2f8b820c7fdf"
}

    "title": "2003001234 sdk v2.1 streaming handshake killflag rollback",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/slack",
    "content": "{\n  \"channel\": \"incidents\",\n  \"thread_ts\": \"2003001234\",\n  \"first_message_ts\": \"2003001234\",\n  \"last_message_ts\": \"2003004389\",\n  \"participants\": [\n    \"inc-bot\",\n    \"alex\",\n    \"maria\",\n    \"chen\",\n    \"sam\",\n    \"joni\",\n    \"carmen\",\n    \"product-pm\",\n    \"ops-bot\"\n  ],\n  \"text\": \"inc-bot: Pager: Elevated error rate (5xx) observed on /v1/streaming endpoints starting ~12:34 UTC after today's SDK rollout. Autoscale OK. Investigating. Tags: release:sdk-v2.1, impact:partial\\n\\nalex: oncall here, looking now. Does this correlate with the 2.1 client handshake change?\\n\\nmaria: yeah that's my canary rollout window. I'm seeing a spike in handshake failures on canary nodes. Reproducing locally against the new client shows client-side frames rejected.\\n\\nchen: pasting recent service logs (handshake errors):\\n```\\n2026-03-15T12:35:10Z runtime[stream-router] ERROR handshake failed: ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH client=svc-frontend-12 src_conn=172.16.4.3\\n2026-03-15T12:35:12Z runtime[stream-router] WARN unexpected frame seq 0x9a expected 0x8\\n2026-03-15T12:35:13Z runtime[stream-router] ERROR upgrade failed: incompatible-client-proto v1->v2\\n```\\n\\nsam: confirmed. The new client (v2.1) changed the initial frame type for streaming init; servers running the new runtime kernel should be backward compatible but older runtime boxes treat it as a protocol mismatch. Canary pool has mixed runtime versions due to staggered deploy.\\n\\njoni: impact? which customers affected and are they in hosted or dedicated?\\n\\ncarmen: looks like hosted streaming customers on region-us-west-2 who use client-side streaming SDKs are seeing partial failures. Non-streaming endpoints (sync generation) appear unaffected. Estimated affected requests ~2-3% of total traffic, but for those flows it's high error rate (50-70%).\\n\\nproduct-pm: any paying customers impacted? we should notify if SLA risk.\\n\\nalex: list of affected customers from telemetry: \\\"playlytics\\\", \\\"chatflow-inc\\\", and a few internal smoke tests. I'll prepare a brief.\\n\\nsam: mitigation options: 1) Kill the feature flag for the new client behavior (ff-sdk-streaming-v2 = off). 2) Pause the SDK rollout. 3) Roll runtime nodes back to previous kernel. Quickest is kill-flag + pause rollout.\\n\\nmaria: I can flip the flag now. This will cause the SDKs to fall back to legacy handshake mode. Rolling back the canary is slower.\\n\\nalex: do it. Share command and ensure deploy bot logs it.\\n\\nmaria: running: `redwood-ffctl set ff-sdk-streaming-v2 false --scope=global --reason=\\\"emergency: handshake errors\\\"`\\n\\nops-bot: Feature flag ff-sdk-streaming-v2 set to false by maria at 2026-03-15T12:39:02Z (reason: emergency: handshake errors).\\n\\ninc-bot: Observability: 1 minute after flag flip, error rate on /v1/streaming dropped by ~85% in affected canary hosts.\\n\\nchen: confirming logs now show handshake success for new incoming clients (back to v1-compatible frames). No more ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH entries in the last 2m.\\n\\nalex: great. Next: pause the client rollout and start rollback of canary group to v2.0 artifact. Who owns that?\\n\\nmaria: I do. Pausing in CI/CD now and initiating rollback for canary subset.\\n\\nmaria: rollback command: `deployctl rollback canary/sdk-client v2.0 --group=canary-assignments --reason=\\\"hotfix: handshake incompat\\\"`\\n\\nops-bot: Rollback started by maria; canary groups will be rolled back over next 10 minutes.\\n\\ncarmen: customer communication: I'll draft a short status update for affected customers: outline symptom, mitigation (FF flipped), expected ETA for full resolution and ask for any error logs.\\n\\nproduct-pm: include that this was caused by a client protocol change that wasn't gated by full runtime compat checks. We're sending an incident notice.\\n\\nalex: oncall handoff note: if this persists beyond rollback window, escalate to eng-runtime pager. Otherwise we'll declare mitigated and do postmortem. Oncall (alex) will own until 14:00 UTC.\\n\\nsam: after rollback completes, we should run a compatibility test matrix: runtime-kernel x client-version handshake matrix across seq lengths and frame types. Add to CI gating.\\n\\njoni: recording immediate action items:\\n- maria: pause rollout + complete rollback (done)\\n- sam: add compat tests to CI gating (owner)\\n- chen: gather logs and prepare timeline (owner)\\n- carmen: customer notices and status page update (owner)\\n- alex: oncall until 14:00 UTC, coordinate postmortem (owner)\\n\\nmaria: rollback completed at 2026-03-15T12:49:07Z. Canary traffic now on v2.0. Flag remains off.\\n\\nops-bot: Monitoring: /v1/streaming 5xx rate returned to baseline across regions. No ongoing alerts in the last 5m.\\n\\ncarmen: posted status update to customers and the status page: \\\"Mitigated: SDK streaming clients may have experienced handshake errors after the v2.1 client rollout. We flipped a feature flag and rolled canary back to v2.0. No further action required from customers. We will follow up with a full postmortem.\\\"\\n\\nproduct-pm: good. Please schedule a blameless postmortem and include a timeline, root cause (protocol change without runtime gating), and remediation (CI gating, FF preflight, rollout checklist).\\n\\nsam: initial root cause: client v2.1 introduced a handshake frame change that assumes runtime supports new frame type; runtime kernel rollout was staggered and some older kernels rejected the frame. Missing automated compatibility check in release pipeline allowed canary mix.\\n\\nchen: I'll attach the logs + heap of traces to the postmortem doc. Also adding a script to detect ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH in canary rollouts.\\n\\nalex: closing summary: mitigated via feature flag + rollback. Customer impact limited to streaming endpoints for a small set of hosted customers. Action items assigned. We'll reconvene for the postmortem tomorrow 09:00 PT. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:\\n\\ninc-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Severity: Sev2. Created incident ticket INC-2026-034. oncall: alex.\\n\\nmaria: adding retrospective note: let's add a canary-level runtime compatibility check that rejects client-artifact promotion if protocol tests fail.\\n\\nproduct-pm: acknowledged. Adding to roadmap: \\\"compatibility preflight for client-runtime rollouts\\\".\\n\\nalex: handing over to next oncall after 14:00 UTC. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and owners.\\n\\ncarmen: thanks all. I'll follow up with customers once postmortem is published.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"channel\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"text\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_2620b91cb0eb413d820a05944ba4dacc\"\n}",

document.content:
{
  "channel": "incidents",
  "thread_ts": "2003001234",
  "first_message_ts": "2003001234",
  "last_message_ts": "2003004389",
  "participants": [
    "inc-bot",
    "alex",
    "maria",
    "chen",
    "sam",
    "joni",
    "carmen",
    "product-pm",
    "ops-bot"
  ],
  "text": "inc-bot: Pager: Elevated error rate (5xx) observed on /v1/streaming endpoints starting ~12:34 UTC after today's SDK rollout. Autoscale OK. Investigating. Tags: release:sdk-v2.1, impact:partial

alex: oncall here, looking now. Does this correlate with the 2.1 client handshake change?

maria: yeah that's my canary rollout window. I'm seeing a spike in handshake failures on canary nodes. Reproducing locally against the new client shows client-side frames rejected.

chen: pasting recent service logs (handshake errors):
```
2026-03-15T12:35:10Z runtime[stream-router] ERROR handshake failed: ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH client=svc-frontend-12 src_conn=172.16.4.3
2026-03-15T12:35:12Z runtime[stream-router] WARN unexpected frame seq 0x9a expected 0x8
2026-03-15T12:35:13Z runtime[stream-router] ERROR upgrade failed: incompatible-client-proto v1->v2
```

sam: confirmed. The new client (v2.1) changed the initial frame type for streaming init; servers running the new runtime kernel should be backward compatible but older runtime boxes treat it as a protocol mismatch. Canary pool has mixed runtime versions due to staggered deploy.

joni: impact? which customers affected and are they in hosted or dedicated?

carmen: looks like hosted streaming customers on region-us-west-2 who use client-side streaming SDKs are seeing partial failures. Non-streaming endpoints (sync generation) appear unaffected. Estimated affected requests ~2-3% of total traffic, but for those flows it's high error rate (50-70%).

product-pm: any paying customers impacted? we should notify if SLA risk.

alex: list of affected customers from telemetry: "playlytics", "chatflow-inc", and a few internal smoke tests. I'll prepare a brief.

sam: mitigation options: 1) Kill the feature flag for the new client behavior (ff-sdk-streaming-v2 = off). 2) Pause the SDK rollout. 3) Roll runtime nodes back to previous kernel. Quickest is kill-flag + pause rollout.

maria: I can flip the flag now. This will cause the SDKs to fall back to legacy handshake mode. Rolling back the canary is slower.

alex: do it. Share command and ensure deploy bot logs it.

maria: running: `redwood-ffctl set ff-sdk-streaming-v2 false --scope=global --reason="emergency: handshake errors"`

ops-bot: Feature flag ff-sdk-streaming-v2 set to false by maria at 2026-03-15T12:39:02Z (reason: emergency: handshake errors).

inc-bot: Observability: 1 minute after flag flip, error rate on /v1/streaming dropped by ~85% in affected canary hosts.

chen: confirming logs now show handshake success for new incoming clients (back to v1-compatible frames). No more ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH entries in the last 2m.

alex: great. Next: pause the client rollout and start rollback of canary group to v2.0 artifact. Who owns that?

maria: I do. Pausing in CI/CD now and initiating rollback for canary subset.

maria: rollback command: `deployctl rollback canary/sdk-client v2.0 --group=canary-assignments --reason="hotfix: handshake incompat"`

ops-bot: Rollback started by maria; canary groups will be rolled back over next 10 minutes.

carmen: customer communication: I'll draft a short status update for affected customers: outline symptom, mitigation (FF flipped), expected ETA for full resolution and ask for any error logs.

product-pm: include that this was caused by a client protocol change that wasn't gated by full runtime compat checks. We're sending an incident notice.

alex: oncall handoff note: if this persists beyond rollback window, escalate to eng-runtime pager. Otherwise we'll declare mitigated and do postmortem. Oncall (alex) will own until 14:00 UTC.

sam: after rollback completes, we should run a compatibility test matrix: runtime-kernel x client-version handshake matrix across seq lengths and frame types. Add to CI gating.

joni: recording immediate action items:
- maria: pause rollout + complete rollback (done)
- sam: add compat tests to CI gating (owner)
- chen: gather logs and prepare timeline (owner)
- carmen: customer notices and status page update (owner)
- alex: oncall until 14:00 UTC, coordinate postmortem (owner)

maria: rollback completed at 2026-03-15T12:49:07Z. Canary traffic now on v2.0. Flag remains off.

ops-bot: Monitoring: /v1/streaming 5xx rate returned to baseline across regions. No ongoing alerts in the last 5m.

carmen: posted status update to customers and the status page: "Mitigated: SDK streaming clients may have experienced handshake errors after the v2.1 client rollout. We flipped a feature flag and rolled canary back to v2.0. No further action required from customers. We will follow up with a full postmortem."

product-pm: good. Please schedule a blameless postmortem and include a timeline, root cause (protocol change without runtime gating), and remediation (CI gating, FF preflight, rollout checklist).

sam: initial root cause: client v2.1 introduced a handshake frame change that assumes runtime supports new frame type; runtime kernel rollout was staggered and some older kernels rejected the frame. Missing automated compatibility check in release pipeline allowed canary mix.

chen: I'll attach the logs + heap of traces to the postmortem doc. Also adding a script to detect ERR_CLIENT_FRAME_MISMATCH in canary rollouts.

alex: closing summary: mitigated via feature flag + rollback. Customer impact limited to streaming endpoints for a small set of hosted customers. Action items assigned. We'll reconvene for the postmortem tomorrow 09:00 PT. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Severity: Sev2. Created incident ticket INC-2026-034. oncall: alex.

maria: adding retrospective note: let's add a canary-level runtime compatibility check that rejects client-artifact promotion if protocol tests fail.

product-pm: acknowledged. Adding to roadmap: "compatibility preflight for client-runtime rollouts".

alex: handing over to next oncall after 14:00 UTC. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and owners.

carmen: thanks all. I'll follow up with customers once postmortem is published.",

    "text"

    "title": "Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) \\u2014 Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds\",\n  \"space\": \"customer-success-and-support\",\n  \"author\": \"Dev Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"customer-success\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-07-18\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-09-05\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Lauren Bishop\",\n    \"Vanessa Ortiz\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"dedicated\",\n    \"autoscaling\",\n    \"predictive-scaling\",\n    \"known-issues\",\n    \"support-playbook\",\n    \"rollout\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/autoscaling-bounds-customer-escalation-playbook.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler-troubleshooting-runbook.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/autoscaling-bounds-observability-dashboard-spec.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/dedicated-autoscaling-bounds-and-predictive-mode-release-notes.json\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"h1. Overview\\nPredictive autoscaling is an opt-in mode for *Redwood Dedicated* that biases scale decisions using forecasted demand (time-of-day patterns, scheduled events, historical request rates/latency). Predictive mode *does not* override customer-configured *min/max bounds* and will fall back to reactive signals when forecasts are stale/unavailable.\\n\\nThis page lists the most common *known issues* observed during pilot/canary, how to recognize them, and recommended *workarounds* for Customer Success and Support. This is not a full runbook; for deep debugging and mitigations, use the dedicated on-call runbook linked above.\\n\\nh2. Scope / When this page applies\\n* Applies to:* Dedicated deployments with predictive mode enabled (feature-flagged per account/deployment).\\n* Not applicable to:* Hosted API autoscaling or Dedicated deployments running reactive-only scaling.\\n\\nh2. Quick definitions (customer-friendly)\\n* *Forecast / prediction:* A projected target capacity (replicas/GPU slices) for an upcoming time window.\\n* *Reactive scaling:* Signals like queue depth, saturation, and latency that trigger scaling based on current conditions.\\n* *Bounds:* Customer-configured *min* and *max* capacity. The autoscaler clamps desired capacity within these bounds.\\n* *Bound-hit:* When the autoscaler wants to go above max or below min but is prevented by bounds.\\n\\nh1. Rollout caveats (read first)\\n1) *Opt-in + guarded rollout:* Predictive mode is still rolling out. Some regions/accounts may not be eligible.\\n2) *Model/workload sensitivity:* Highly bursty workloads with low steady-state traffic can produce noisy forecasts.\\n3) *Do not promise \\u201cno queueing\\u201d under max bounds:* If traffic exceeds max-bound capacity and the region cannot burst, queueing/latency can occur. This is expected behavior; the product surfaces it via bound-hit metrics.\\n4) *Time-to-effect:* Changes to predictive settings may take up to *10\\u201320 minutes* to reflect in decisions (depending on caching and evaluation intervals).\\n\\nh1. Known issues & workarounds\\n\\nh2. 1) False positives (over-scaling before traffic arrives)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Capacity ramps up early; customer sees increased spend/idle utilization.\\n* Forecast line is above actual demand; prediction error is consistently positive.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Holidays/product changes make recent history unrepresentative.\\n* Scheduled-event definitions are too broad (e.g., daily job marked as \\u201chigh\\u201d when it is moderate).\\n* Low-volume workloads where small absolute errors become large relative errors.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) *Reduce predictive bias* (preferred): switch to \\u201cPredictive + Reactive Override\\u201d (if available in the customer\\u2019s build) or lower the predictive weight via internal config (eng-assisted).\\n2) *Use a tighter max bound* to cap spend if the customer\\u2019s primary concern is budget.\\n3) If customer can tolerate brief queueing, recommend *reactive-only* during the window and re-enable predictive after retraining/after a week of stable traffic.\\n\\n*Support notes*\\n* Collect: deployment_id, region, last 7 days of request rate, and a screenshot of desired vs bounded capacity.\\n* If the customer is in contract negotiation over cost ceilings, steer toward bounds and recommended ranges, not predictive promises.\\n\\nh2. 2) Timezone misalignment (forecast ramps at the wrong local time)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Customer reports \\u201cit scales for our ramp, but 1\\u20133 hours too early/late.\\u201d\\n* Recurring daily ramp shows a consistent offset.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Traffic exhibits local-time patterns but the forecast is effectively aligned to UTC (or mis-tagged timezone).\\n* Scheduled events were provided in local time but entered/processed as UTC.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Confirm the customer\\u2019s *operational timezone* and the timezone assumed for any scheduled events.\\n2) Temporary mitigation: set a *higher min bound* covering the ramp window until timezone is corrected.\\n3) If the account uses scheduled events: update the event schedule with explicit timezone (eng-assisted if the UI/API does not expose timezone selection yet).\\n\\n*Escalation trigger*\\n* If offset is consistent and reproducible, file an escalation to Eng Infra with: account_id, deployment_id, region, customer timezone, and at least two days of graphs showing the offset.\\n\\nh2. 3) Insufficient history (under-scaling because the predictor lacks training data)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Predictive mode enabled, but scaling behaves similar to reactive-only.\\n* Forecast confidence is low or \\u201cnot available\\u201d; autoscaler logs indicate fallback to reactive.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* New deployment or new model route without enough steady history.\\n* Major traffic shape change in the last few days.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Set a *conservative min bound* aligned to baseline throughput to avoid cold starts.\\n2) Use *reactive-only* for the first 1\\u20132 weeks of a new deployment, then re-enable predictive mode once traffic stabilizes.\\n3) If ramp is known and contractual, use *scheduled events* (if enabled for the account) as an interim signal source.\\n\\n*Support note*\\n* \\u201cPredictive mode\\u201d is not a guarantee; it is a best-effort bias that requires stable patterns.\\n\\nh2. 4) Stale forecast / prediction pipeline outage (sudden behavior change)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Predictive scaling appears to stop; capacity only changes after queue depth increases.\\n* UI shows forecast timestamp is old, or \\u201cforecast unavailable.\\u201d\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Forecast provider returned stale data; the autoscaler rejected it due to staleness checks.\\n* Regional data pipeline delay.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Treat as expected fail-safe: *reactive scaling takes over*.\\n2) Raise min bound temporarily for the affected ramp window.\\n3) If customer is impacted (p95 latency regression), advise disabling predictive mode until pipeline recovers.\\n\\n*Escalation trigger*\\n* Any incident where stale forecasts correlate with user-visible latency/SLO breach: escalate to SRE per the Dedicated autoscaler runbook.\\n\\nh2. 5) Oscillation / capacity jitter (scale up/down thrash)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Replicas/GPU count changes frequently (e.g., every few minutes).\\n* Customer sees request latency jitter; autoscaler event stream shows alternating scale-up and scale-down.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* Noisy predictions combined with aggressive cooldowns.\\n* Workload has spiky batch traffic that looks like repeated ramps.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Increase *cooldown* / dampening parameters (eng-assisted if not customer-configurable yet).\\n2) Increase *min step size* for scale changes (avoid micro-adjustments).\\n3) Prefer reactive signals for scale-down, predictive for scale-up (hybrid mode) where available.\\n4) If the customer is latency-sensitive, disable predictive temporarily and stabilize with min bound.\\n\\n*Support note*\\n* If a pilot customer reports oscillation, check whether they are on the build containing anti-oscillation guardrails. If not, coordinate an upgrade or disable predictive.\\n\\nh2. 6) Null/empty prediction edge case (unsafe downscale risk)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* A forecast response contains null/empty values; desired capacity appears to drop unexpectedly.\\n\\n*Status*\\n* Mitigated by a hotfix to prevent scale-to-zero when predictor returns null. Some older pilot environments may not have the fix.\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) If suspected: disable predictive mode immediately and set min bound to a safe baseline.\\n2) Escalate to Eng Infra with urgency and include timestamps + deployment_id.\\n\\nh2. 7) Max-bound saturation (predictive wants more capacity than allowed)\\n*Symptoms*\\n* Queue depth increases during ramp; customer sees \\u201cwe told it to scale, but it didn\\u2019t.\\u201d\\n* Metrics show frequent *max-bound hit* events.\\n\\n*Likely causes*\\n* The customer\\u2019s max bound is below what the workload requires for the ramp.\\n* Region capacity shortage prevents provisioning even below max (rare but possible).\\n\\n*Recommended workarounds*\\n1) Clarify intent: if max bound is a *hard budget cap*, then queueing is an expected tradeoff.\\n2) If customer goal is SLA/latency, recommend increasing max bound or using burst capacity (if contract allows).\\n3) For predictable ramps: raise min bound ahead of the ramp so the system is already warm.\\n\\n*Escalation trigger*\\n* If min bound cannot be met due to region shortage, treat as a reliability event (see shortage behavior in the runbook).\\n\\nh1. What to ask the customer (minimum checklist)\\n1) Deployment name / deployment_id and region\\n2) Current bounds: min, max, cooldowns (if known)\\n3) Predictive mode state (enabled? hybrid? scheduled events?)\\n4) The customer\\u2019s local timezone and the time window of the ramp\\n5) Impact statement: spend concern vs latency/SLA concern\\n6) Screenshots or exports of: desired vs bounded capacity, queue depth, and p95 latency over the affected window\\n\\nh1. Recommended customer guidance (safe, non-committal language)\\n* \\u201cPredictive autoscaling helps pre-warm capacity for repeating traffic patterns, but it still respects your min/max bounds and will fall back to reactive scaling when forecasts are not available.\\u201d\\n* \\u201cIf the primary goal is controlling spend, set a max bound you\\u2019re comfortable with and we can tune predictive behavior to avoid early ramp-ups.\\u201d\\n* \\u201cIf the primary goal is meeting latency SLO during a known ramp, a higher baseline min (or scheduled event) is often the most reliable first step.\\u201d\\n\\nh1. When to escalate (internal)\\nEscalate to *Eng Infra / SRE* if any of the following are true:\\n* Predictive mode enabled and customer reports sustained latency regression (p95/p99) during a known ramp\\n* Reproducible timezone offset or consistently stale forecasts\\n* Oscillation causing user-visible impact\\n* Suspected null/empty prediction edge case\\n* Min bound cannot be met (possible region shortage)\\n\\nInclude in escalation: account_id, deployment_id, region, timestamps, graphs for queue depth + desired/bounded capacity, and whether disabling predictive mitigates.\\n\\nh1. Changelog\\n* 2025-09-05: Updated mitigations for oscillation and clarified max-bound saturation guidance.\\n* 2025-08-02: Added null/empty prediction edge case and mitigation instructions.\\n* 2025-07-18: Initial publication for pilot support readiness.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_07daff0e8966460f86c297b6939b607a\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/predictive-autoscaling-known-issues.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: customer-success-and-support\n\nconfidentiality : internal body : h1. overview predictive autoscaling is an opt - in mode for * redwood dedicated * that biases scale decisions using forecasted demand ( time - of - day patterns, scheduled events, historical request rates / latency ). predictive mode * does not * override customer - configured * min / max bounds * and will fall back to reactive signals when forecasts are stale / unavailable. this page lists the most common * known issues * observed during pilot / canary, how to recognize them, and recommended * workarounds * for customer success and support. this is not a full runbook ; for deep debugging and mitigations, use the dedicated on - call runbook linked above.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/predictive-autoscaling-known-issues.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: customer-success-and-support\n\n- only. * forecast confidence is low or “ not available ” ; autoscaler logs indicate fallback to reactive. * likely causes * * new deployment or new model route without enough steady history. * major traffic shape change in the last few days. * recommended workarounds * 1 ) set a * conservative min bound * aligned to baseline throughput to avoid cold starts. 2 ) use * reactive - only * for the first 1 – 2 weeks of a new deployment, then re - enable predictive mode once traffic stabilizes. 3 ) if ramp is known and contractual, use * scheduled events * ( if enabled for the account ) as an interim signal source.",

document.content:
{
  "title": "Predictive Autoscaling (Dedicated) — Known Issues & Recommended Workarounds",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Dev Patel",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-07-18",
  "last_updated": "2025-09-05",
  "reviewers": [
    "Lauren Bishop",
    "Vanessa Ortiz",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Allison Grant"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "dedicated",
    "autoscaling",
    "predictive-scaling",
    "known-issues",
    "support-playbook",
    "rollout"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/autoscaling-bounds-customer-escalation-playbook.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler-troubleshooting-runbook.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/autoscaling-bounds-observability-dashboard-spec.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-autoscaling-bounds-precedence-and-safety-invariants.json",
    "sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/dedicated-autoscaling-bounds-and-predictive-mode-release-notes.json"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "h1. Overview
Predictive autoscaling is an opt-in mode for *Redwood Dedicated* that biases scale decisions using forecasted demand (time-of-day patterns, scheduled events, historical request rates/latency). Predictive mode *does not* override customer-configured *min/max bounds* and will fall back to reactive signals when forecasts are stale/unavailable.

This page lists the most common *known issues* observed during pilot/canary, how to recognize them, and recommended *workarounds* for Customer Success and Support. This is not a full runbook; for deep debugging and mitigations, use the dedicated on-call runbook linked above.

h2. Scope / When this page applies
* Applies to:* Dedicated deployments with predictive mode enabled (feature-flagged per account/deployment).
* Not applicable to:* Hosted API autoscaling or Dedicated deployments running reactive-only scaling.

h2. Quick definitions (customer-friendly)
* *Forecast / prediction:* A projected target capacity (replicas/GPU slices) for an upcoming time window.
* *Reactive scaling:* Signals like queue depth, saturation, and latency that trigger scaling based on current conditions.
* *Bounds:* Customer-configured *min* and *max* capacity. The autoscaler clamps desired capacity within these bounds.
* *Bound-hit:* When the autoscaler wants to go above max or below min but is prevented by bounds.

h1. Rollout caveats (read first)
1) *Opt-in + guarded rollout:* Predictive mode is still rolling out. Some regions/accounts may not be eligible.
2) *Model/workload sensitivity:* Highly bursty workloads with low steady-state traffic can produce noisy forecasts.
3) *Do not promise “no queueing” under max bounds:* If traffic exceeds max-bound capacity and the region cannot burst, queueing/latency can occur. This is expected behavior; the product surfaces it via bound-hit metrics.
4) *Time-to-effect:* Changes to predictive settings may take up to *10–20 minutes* to reflect in decisions (depending on caching and evaluation intervals).

h1. Known issues & workarounds

h2. 1) False positives (over-scaling before traffic arrives)
*Symptoms*
* Capacity ramps up early; customer sees increased spend/idle utilization.
* Forecast line is above actual demand; prediction error is consistently positive.

*Likely causes*
* Holidays/product changes make recent history unrepresentative.
* Scheduled-event definitions are too broad (e.g., daily job marked as “high” when it is moderate).
* Low-volume workloads where small absolute errors become large relative errors.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) *Reduce predictive bias* (preferred): switch to “Predictive + Reactive Override” (if available in the customer’s build) or lower the predictive weight via internal config (eng-assisted).
2) *Use a tighter max bound* to cap spend if the customer’s primary concern is budget.
3) If customer can tolerate brief queueing, recommend *reactive-only* during the window and re-enable predictive after retraining/after a week of stable traffic.

*Support notes*
* Collect: deployment_id, region, last 7 days of request rate, and a screenshot of desired vs bounded capacity.
* If the customer is in contract negotiation over cost ceilings, steer toward bounds and recommended ranges, not predictive promises.

h2. 2) Timezone misalignment (forecast ramps at the wrong local time)
*Symptoms*
* Customer reports “it scales for our ramp, but 1–3 hours too early/late.”
* Recurring daily ramp shows a consistent offset.

*Likely causes*
* Traffic exhibits local-time patterns but the forecast is effectively aligned to UTC (or mis-tagged timezone).
* Scheduled events were provided in local time but entered/processed as UTC.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Confirm the customer’s *operational timezone* and the timezone assumed for any scheduled events.
2) Temporary mitigation: set a *higher min bound* covering the ramp window until timezone is corrected.
3) If the account uses scheduled events: update the event schedule with explicit timezone (eng-assisted if the UI/API does not expose timezone selection yet).

*Escalation trigger*
* If offset is consistent and reproducible, file an escalation to Eng Infra with: account_id, deployment_id, region, customer timezone, and at least two days of graphs showing the offset.

h2. 3) Insufficient history (under-scaling because the predictor lacks training data)
*Symptoms*
* Predictive mode enabled, but scaling behaves similar to reactive-only.
* Forecast confidence is low or “not available”; autoscaler logs indicate fallback to reactive.

*Likely causes*
* New deployment or new model route without enough steady history.
* Major traffic shape change in the last few days.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Set a *conservative min bound* aligned to baseline throughput to avoid cold starts.
2) Use *reactive-only* for the first 1–2 weeks of a new deployment, then re-enable predictive mode once traffic stabilizes.
3) If ramp is known and contractual, use *scheduled events* (if enabled for the account) as an interim signal source.

*Support note*
* “Predictive mode” is not a guarantee; it is a best-effort bias that requires stable patterns.

h2. 4) Stale forecast / prediction pipeline outage (sudden behavior change)
*Symptoms*
* Predictive scaling appears to stop; capacity only changes after queue depth increases.
* UI shows forecast timestamp is old, or “forecast unavailable.”

*Likely causes*
* Forecast provider returned stale data; the autoscaler rejected it due to staleness checks.
* Regional data pipeline delay.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Treat as expected fail-safe: *reactive scaling takes over*.
2) Raise min bound temporarily for the affected ramp window.
3) If customer is impacted (p95 latency regression), advise disabling predictive mode until pipeline recovers.

*Escalation trigger*
* Any incident where stale forecasts correlate with user-visible latency/SLO breach: escalate to SRE per the Dedicated autoscaler runbook.

h2. 5) Oscillation / capacity jitter (scale up/down thrash)
*Symptoms*
* Replicas/GPU count changes frequently (e.g., every few minutes).
* Customer sees request latency jitter; autoscaler event stream shows alternating scale-up and scale-down.

*Likely causes*
* Noisy predictions combined with aggressive cooldowns.
* Workload has spiky batch traffic that looks like repeated ramps.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Increase *cooldown* / dampening parameters (eng-assisted if not customer-configurable yet).
2) Increase *min step size* for scale changes (avoid micro-adjustments).
3) Prefer reactive signals for scale-down, predictive for scale-up (hybrid mode) where available.
4) If the customer is latency-sensitive, disable predictive temporarily and stabilize with min bound.

*Support note*
* If a pilot customer reports oscillation, check whether they are on the build containing anti-oscillation guardrails. If not, coordinate an upgrade or disable predictive.

h2. 6) Null/empty prediction edge case (unsafe downscale risk)
*Symptoms*
* A forecast response contains null/empty values; desired capacity appears to drop unexpectedly.

*Status*
* Mitigated by a hotfix to prevent scale-to-zero when predictor returns null. Some older pilot environments may not have the fix.

*Recommended workarounds*
1) If suspected: disable predictive mode immediately and set min bound to a safe baseline.
2) Escalate to Eng Infra with urgency and include timestamps + deployment_id.

h2. 7) Max-bound saturation (predictive wants more capacity than allowed)
*Symptoms*
* Queue depth increases during ramp; customer sees “we told it to scale, but it didn’t.”
* Metrics show frequent *max-bound hit* events.

*Likely causes*
* The customer’s max bound is below what the workload requires for the ramp.
* Region capacity shortage prevents provisioning even below max (rare but possible).

*Recommended workarounds*
1) Clarify intent: if max bound is a *hard budget cap*, then queueing is an expected tradeoff.
2) If customer goal is SLA/latency, recommend increasing max bound or using burst capacity (if contract allows).
3) For predictable ramps: raise min bound ahead of the ramp so the system is already warm.

*Escalation trigger*
* If min bound cannot be met due to region shortage, treat as a reliability event (see shortage behavior in the runbook).

h1. What to ask the customer (minimum checklist)
1) Deployment name / deployment_id and region
2) Current bounds: min, max, cooldowns (if known)
3) Predictive mode state (enabled? hybrid? scheduled events?)
4) The customer’s local timezone and the time window of the ramp
5) Impact statement: spend concern vs latency/SLA concern
6) Screenshots or exports of: desired vs bounded capacity, queue depth, and p95 latency over the affected window

h1. Recommended customer guidance (safe, non-committal language)
* “Predictive autoscaling helps pre-warm capacity for repeating traffic patterns, but it still respects your min/max bounds and will fall back to reactive scaling when forecasts are not available.”
* “If the primary goal is controlling spend, set a max bound you’re comfortable with and we can tune predictive behavior to avoid early ramp-ups.”
* “If the primary goal is meeting latency SLO during a known ramp, a higher baseline min (or scheduled event) is often the most reliable first step.”

h1. When to escalate (internal)
Escalate to *Eng Infra / SRE* if any of the following are true:
* Predictive mode enabled and customer reports sustained latency regression (p95/p99) during a known ramp
* Reproducible timezone offset or consistently stale forecasts
* Oscillation causing user-visible impact
* Suspected null/empty prediction edge case
* Min bound cannot be met (possible region shortage)

Include in escalation: account_id, deployment_id, region, timestamps, graphs for queue depth + desired/bounded capacity, and whether disabling predictive mitigates.

h1. Changelog
* 2025-09-05: Updated mitigations for oscillation and clarified max-bound saturation guidance.
* 2025-08-02: Added null/empty prediction edge case and mitigation instructions.
* 2025-07-18: Initial publication for pilot support readiness.",

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"SUP-842631\",\n  \"project\": \"customer-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Incident\",\n  \"summary\": \"Intermittent GPU oversubscription and tail-latency during scheduled batch window for HeliosAI dedicated pool\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-14\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Nina Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Lucas Romero\",\n  \"customer_company\": \"HeliosAI\",\n  \"customer_tier\": \"dedicated\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"serving-runtime\",\n    \"autoscaler\",\n    \"scheduler\",\n    \"observability\",\n    \"dedicated-capacity\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"noisy-neighbor\",\n    \"gpu-starvation\",\n    \"autoscale\",\n    \"p99-latency\",\n    \"investigating\",\n    \"scheduled-window\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod-us-west-2\",\n  \"affected_models\": [\n    \"gptx-24b-v2\",\n    \"embedx-1024\"\n  ],\n  \"affected_regions\": [\n    \"us-west-2\"\n  ],\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2026-03-12T18:00:00Z\",\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2026-03-12T13:00:00Z\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"SUP-33489\",\n    \"SUP-631210\"\n  ],\n  \"related_github_prs\": [\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4182\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RINF/Dedicated+Autoscale+Runbook\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary:\\nHeliosAI is reporting repeated p99 latency spikes and request queuing in their dedicated GPU pool that coincide with a daily scheduled batch window (12:00-12:30 PDT). Symptoms look like ephemeral GPU oversubscription and batch slot thrashing rather than model regression.\\n\\nImpact:\\n- Customer reports increased p99 generation latency from ~400ms to >3s during scheduled window.\\n- Failed requests (5xx) are low but queued latency causes timeouts for streaming clients.\\n- Business impact: degraded user experience for HeliosAI production customers during a predictable 30-minute window.\\n\\nEnvironment:\\n- Dedicated pool: helios-dedicated-pool-3 (5 x A100:80GB equivalent nodes)\\n- Region: us-west-2\\n- Models: gptx-24b-v2 (primary), embedx-1024 (background embedding jobs)\\n\\nTimeline (customer-supplied):\\n- 2026-03-11 19:00 UTC: First report of tail latency during scheduled batch run.\\n- 2026-03-12 19:25 UTC: Customer escalated after repeated occurrences over two days.\\n\\nObserved behavior:\\n- Sustained queue growth during 12:00-12:30 PDT each day.\\n- Autoscaler shows transient spike in pending pods/slots that are not immediately reconciled.\\n- GPU utilization reports show per-GPU average ~70% but per-tenant slot contention and bursty kernel launches.\\n- KV cache growth for gptx-24b-v2 correlates to an increase in memory pressure on a subset of nodes.\\n\\nExpected behavior:\\n- Autoscaler should provision capacity ahead of steady scheduled load or apply predictive headroom to avoid p99 spikes.\\n- No single tenant should cause transient oversubscription of GPU batching lanes in a dedicated pool.\\n\\nWorkaround attempted by customer:\\n- Staggered batch start times (reduced but did not eliminate spikes).\\n- Reduced concurrency per client which lowered p99 but increased overall run time for batch job.\\n\\nAdditional notes:\\n- This is not a global capacity shortage; other dedicated pools in us-west-2 are unaffected.\\n- Appears related to tenant-level workload pattern (short, high-concurrency embedding bursts mixed with long-generation sessions).\",\n  \"steps_to_reproduce\": \"1) Customer schedules concurrent embedding job burst at 12:00 PDT targeting embedx-1024 with high concurrency.\\n2) At same time, several long-running streaming generation sessions to gptx-24b-v2 remain warm.\\n3) Observe autoscaler activity (pending slots, allocation latency) and request queue growth in dedicated pool helios-dedicated-pool-3.\\n4) Check p99 latency and GPU kernel launch patterns during window.\",\n  \"logs\": \"[2026-03-12T19:24:08Z] scheduler: slot_request queued tenant=heliosai job=embed-burst-321 size=64\\n[2026-03-12T19:24:10Z] autoscaler: attempt_allocate pool=helios-dedicated-pool-3 pending=8 available_nodes=2\\n[2026-03-12T19:24:12Z] serving-runtime: batcher: serialize_delay=120ms tenant=heliosai route=/v1/generate model=gptx-24b-v2\\n[2026-03-12T19:24:14Z] telemetry: p99_latency=3200ms tenant=heliosai route=/v1/generate\\n[2026-03-12T19:24:17Z] gpu-metrics: node=node-07 nvlink_io_wait=45% kernel_queue_depth=12\\n[2026-03-12T19:24:20Z] kvcache: growth=+1.6GB tenant=heliosai model=gptx-24b-v2\\n\",\n  \"investigation_notes\": [\n    \"2026-03-12 20:00 UTC - Initial triage by Support: Confirmed scheduled window alignment and repeated pattern. No cluster-wide capacity alarms.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 21:10 UTC - Observability: Identified subset of nodes (node-06, node-07) showing elevated nvlink_io_wait and kernel_queue_depth spikes coincident with queue growth.\",\n    \"2026-03-13 02:05 UTC - Hypothesis A: Noisy tenant pattern from embedding burst is consuming batching lanes and causing head-of-line blocking for generation requests on same GPUs.\",\n    \"2026-03-13 04:20 UTC - Hypothesis B: KV cache growth for gptx-24b-v2 pushes memory pressure, triggering micro-evictions and increased kernel warmup latencies on affected GPUs.\",\n    \"2026-03-13 10:30 UTC - Autoscaler logs show allocation attempts delayed by ~30s during peak pending spike, suggesting reconciliation lag under bursty demand.\",\n    \"2026-03-13 14:00 UTC - Correlation with tenant affinity: customer jobs have affinity hints leading scheduler to colocate embedding burst and generation sessions on same nodes to leverage warm context; this increases contention.\",\n    \"\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"Nina Patel (Support) 2026-03-12 19:45 UTC: Acknowledged with customer, requested exact cron/batch job start times and recent request traces. Asked for request_id samples.\",\n    \"HeliosAI (Customer) 2026-03-12 20:05 UTC: Provided cron=0 19 * * * (12:00 PDT) and three request_ids: r_8a1f2, r_8a1f3, r_8a1f4. Noted the embedding burst uses concurrency 64 across 8 workers.\",\n    \"Lucas Romero (SRE) 2026-03-12 21:30 UTC: Investigating node-level NVLink metrics and kernel queue depths. Marked for deeper GPU telemetry pull and batcher sampling.\",\n    \"Lucas Romero (SRE) 2026-03-13 02:15 UTC: Observed kernel_queue_depth spikes on node-06/07. Requested temporary mitigation: advise customer to stagger embedding job by 2 minutes while we collect traces.\",\n    \"HeliosAI (Customer) 2026-03-13 02:40 UTC: Agreed to stagger for next run (will start at 12:02 PDT). Will provide telemetry if behavior changes.\",\n    \"Nina Patel (Support) 2026-03-13 14:10 UTC: Noted that staggering reduced p99 by ~35% but did not eliminate spikes; escalated to runtime/allocator team.\",\n    \"Runtime Team (Eng) 2026-03-14 08:20 UTC: Proposed short-term patch to scheduler to honor tenant-level spread for concurrent jobs (avoid strict affinity during scheduled windows). Testing on canary pool.\",\n    \"SRE (Eng) 2026-03-14 11:05 UTC: Canary run shows improvement for mixed workloads; patch reduces NVLink contention on canary nodes by ~30%.\",\n    \"\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": \"1) Apply scheduler spread mitigation to customer pool during next scheduled window as a targeted config (controlled rollout).\\n2) Add predictive headroom to autoscaler for known scheduled windows (customer-configurable).\\n3) Instrument more granular kernel and NVLink telemetry for dedicated pools to attribute noisy-tenant behaviour precisely.\\n4) Follow up with HeliosAI after two successful windows to validate fix and discuss longer-term rate-limiting/priority controls.\",\n  \"resolution\": \"In Progress - Temporary mitigation applied in canary. Plan to roll targeted scheduler spread to helios-dedicated-pool-3 for next maintenance window. No permanent fix yet; engineering assigned to runtime scheduler and autoscaler teams.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"steps_to_reproduce\",\n    \"logs\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"next_steps\",\n    \"resolution\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_8941e18b540a4a5283be8f5ccbeb7f00\"\n}",

  "description": "Issue summary:\nHeliosAI is reporting repeated p99 latency spikes and request queuing in their dedicated GPU pool that coincide with a daily scheduled batch window (12:00-12:30 PDT). Symptoms look like ephemeral GPU oversubscription and batch slot thrashing rather than model regression.\n\nImpact:\n- Customer reports increased p99 generation latency from ~400ms to >3s during scheduled window.\n- Failed requests (5xx) are low but queued latency causes timeouts for streaming clients.\n- Business impact: degraded user experience for HeliosAI production customers during a predictable 30-minute window.\n\nEnvironment:\n- Dedicated pool: helios-dedicated-pool-3 (5 x A100:80GB equivalent nodes)\n- Region: us-west-2\n- Models: gptx-24b-v2 (primary), embedx-1024 (background embedding jobs)\n\nTimeline (customer-supplied):\n- 2026-03-11 19:00 UTC: First report of tail latency during scheduled batch run.\n- 2026-03-12 19:25 UTC: Customer escalated after repeated occurrences over two days.\n\nObserved behavior:\n- Sustained queue growth during 12:00-12:30 PDT each day.\n- Autoscaler shows transient spike in pending pods/slots that are not immediately reconciled.\n- GPU utilization reports show per-GPU average ~70% but per-tenant slot contention and bursty kernel launches.\n- KV cache growth for gptx-24b-v2 correlates to an increase in memory pressure on a subset of nodes.\n\nExpected behavior:\n- Autoscaler should provision capacity ahead of steady scheduled load or apply predictive headroom to avoid p99 spikes.\n- No single tenant should cause transient oversubscription of GPU batching lanes in a dedicated pool.\n\nWorkaround attempted by customer:\n- Staggered batch start times (reduced but did not eliminate spikes).\n- Reduced concurrency per client which lowered p99 but increased overall run time for batch job.\n\nAdditional notes:\n- This is not a global capacity shortage; other dedicated pools in us-west-2 are unaffected.\n- Appears related to tenant-level workload pattern (short, high-concurrency embedding bursts mixed with long-generation sessions).",

  "logs": "[2026-03-12T19:24:08Z] scheduler: slot_request queued tenant=heliosai job=embed-burst-321 size=64\n[2026-03-12T19:24:10Z] autoscaler: attempt_allocate pool=helios-dedicated-pool-3 pending=8 available_nodes=2\n[2026-03-12T19:24:12Z] serving-runtime: batcher: serialize_delay=120ms tenant=heliosai route=/v1/generate model=gptx-24b-v2\n[2026-03-12T19:24:14Z] telemetry: p99_latency=3200ms tenant=heliosai route=/v1/generate\n[2026-03-12T19:24:17Z] gpu-metrics: node=node-07 nvlink_io_wait=45% kernel_queue_depth=12\n[2026-03-12T19:24:20Z] kvcache: growth=+1.6GB tenant=heliosai model=gptx-24b-v2\n",

    "2026-03-12 20:00 UTC - Initial triage by Support: Confirmed scheduled window alignment and repeated pattern. No cluster-wide capacity alarms.",
    "2026-03-12 21:10 UTC - Observability: Identified subset of nodes (node-06, node-07) showing elevated nvlink_io_wait and kernel_queue_depth spikes coincident with queue growth.",
    "2026-03-13 02:05 UTC - Hypothesis A: Noisy tenant pattern from embedding burst is consuming batching lanes and causing head-of-line blocking for generation requests on same GPUs.",
    "2026-03-13 04:20 UTC - Hypothesis B: KV cache growth for gptx-24b-v2 pushes memory pressure, triggering micro-evictions and increased kernel warmup latencies on affected GPUs.",
    "2026-03-13 10:30 UTC - Autoscaler logs show allocation attempts delayed by ~30s during peak pending spike, suggesting reconciliation lag under bursty demand.",

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_a3fdfc45905f46f3988ad13f55ecce93",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-428317-conditional-multitenant-ratelimiter-priority-skew.json",
    "title": "Conditional multitenant rate limiter priority skew causing transient under-enforcement",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"ENG-428317\",\n  \"team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"title\": \"Conditional multitenant rate limiter priority skew causing transient under-enforcement\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-14\",\n  \"creator\": \"Lina Chen\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marco Ruiz\",\n  \"project\": \"RateEngine 2.0 - correctness\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2026-Q1-Cycle 5\",\n  \"estimate\": \"5\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-03-21\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"billing\",\n    \"rate-limiter\",\n    \"investigation\",\n    \"high-impact\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Intermittent cases where per-key priority overrides combined with per-org and per-route policies result in transient under-enforcement (requests allowed when they should be throttled). Observed as short windows of elevated usage for a small set of tenants after shard reassignment and policy hot-reload. This ticket captures investigation, repro, short-term mitigation, and a long-term fix plan.\",\n  \"reproduction_steps\": [\n    \"1) Create two tenants T1 and T2 sharing a shard (sticky-shard assignment enabled).\",\n    \"2) Configure per-org policy: default priority = low, per-route quota = 1000/min.\",\n    \"3) Configure per-key override for a service key K1 belonging to T1: priority = high, burst credits = +200.\",\n    \"4) Start a steady stream of requests from T1 at near-quota rate; verify enforcement hitting quota windows.\",\n    \"5) Trigger a shard reassignment for one edge node (simulate instance bounce or maintenance) while simultaneously applying a policy hot-reload that changes route fallback behavior.\",\n    \"6) Observe a ~10-30s window where requests for K1 are allowed beyond quota; metrics show credits attributed to the wrong in-memory bucket and enforcement checks returning allow from fast-path cache.\",\n    \"7) Collect tracer spans and edge logs for the window; reproduce locally using the shard-reassignment harness and time-accelerated policy reloads.\"\n  ],\n  \"impact\": \"Transient over-allow for small number of tenants leading to underbilling and potential customer perception issues; visible as short-lived bursts up to ~2x expected throughput for affected keys. Affects hosted and dedicated clusters during rolling updates or instance restarts.\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"logs_snapshot\": [\n    \"edge: allow decision fastpath: key=K1 shard=sh-23 cache_hit=true priority=high quota_window_id=2026-03-12T10:04:00Z\",\n    \"shard-reassign: lease=renewal failover->sh-27 old_owner=sh-23 new_owner=sh-27\",\n    \"policy-hot-reload: version=v2026-03-12-1 route-fallback=enabled\",\n    \"meter-commit: credits_applied target_bucket=org:T2:key:Kx unexpected=true amount=200\"\n  ],\n  \"hypothesis\": \"A race between sticky-shard mapping update and policy hot-reload causes fast-path cache entries (priority and credit pointers) to be re-keyed incorrectly. Per-key overrides store a pointer to a tenant-scoped credit bucket; during reassignment we are dereferencing a stale pointer and applying credits to the wrong tenant's bucket. Enforcement uses the fast-path decision if cache present, so the wrong credits cause an allow where a deny should occur.\",\n  \"experiment_results\": \"Replayed the sequence in staging using the shard-reassign harness. With no policy reload the issue did not occur. When timed policy reload coincided with reassignment, we reproduced the over-allow consistently. Enabling stronger pointer validation (temporary patch) eliminated the over-allows in the harness.\",\n  \"root_cause\": \"Sticky-shard pointer (in-memory bucket reference) is validated only by shard id but not by tenant id during fast-path credit application. Policy hot-reload mutates the route/priority indices while a shard transfer copies pointers; combined these can produce a transient pointer that points at an unrelated tenant's bucket. Enforcement fast-path accepts the cache without full tenant-level validation.\",\n  \"mitigations\": \"Short-term patch deployed to staging: on fast-path cache hit, perform tenant-id validation on the cached credit pointer before applying credits. Also increased grace period on shard handoff to reduce overlap. Rolled patch to canary edge fleet.\",\n  \"rollout_plan\": \"1) Canary for 2 hours on low-traffic region with added telemetry (done). 2) Gradual ramp to 30% of traffic with continued trace sampling for next 24 hours. 3) Full rollout after 48 hours if no regressions. 4) Follow with a database reconciliation backfill job to detect credits misapplied in last 7 days and create accounting fixes if needed.\",\n  \"long_term_fix\": \"Refactor in-memory credit pointer representation to be immutable and namespaced by tenant+shard+route. Replace pointer dereference fast-path with a lightweight validation token check (versioned binder). Add unit and property tests for concurrent shard handoff + policy reload scenarios.\",\n  \"regression_test_plan\": \"Add deterministic concurrency tests to runtime-policy-simulator: combinations of shard reassignment, policy hot-reload, per-key overrides, and burst credit application. Add e2e test in CI harness that exercises rolling updates with randomized interleavings. document.title: Conditional multitenant rate limiter priority skew causing transient under-enforcement
document.content:
{
  "key": "ENG-428317",
  "team": "engineering",
  "title": "Conditional multitenant rate limiter priority skew causing transient under-enforcement",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-12",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-14",
  "creator": "Lina Chen",
  "assignee": "Marco Ruiz",
  "project": "RateEngine 2.0 - correctness",
  "cycle": "2026-Q1-Cycle 5",
  "estimate": "5",
  "due_date": "2026-03-21",
  "labels": [
    "billing",
    "rate-limiter",
    "investigation",
    "high-impact"
  ],
  "description": "Intermittent cases where per-key priority overrides combined with per-org and per-route policies result in transient under-enforcement (requests allowed when they should be throttled). Observed as short windows of elevated usage for a small set of tenants after shard reassignment and policy hot-reload. This ticket captures investigation, repro, short-term mitigation, and a long-term fix plan.",
  "reproduction_steps": [
    "1) Create two tenants T1 and T2 sharing a shard (sticky-shard assignment enabled).",
    "2) Configure per-org policy: default priority = low, per-route quota = 1000/min.",
    "3) Configure per-key override for a service key K1 belonging to T1: priority = high, burst credits = +200.",
    "4) Start a steady stream of requests from T1 at near-quota rate; verify enforcement hitting quota windows.",
    "5) Trigger a shard reassignment for one edge node (simulate instance bounce or maintenance) while simultaneously applying a policy hot-reload that changes route fallback behavior.",
    "6) Observe a ~10-30s window where requests for K1 are allowed beyond quota; metrics show credits attributed to the wrong in-memory bucket and enforcement checks returning allow from fast-path cache.",
    "7) Collect tracer spans and edge logs for the window; reproduce locally using the shard-reassignment harness and time-accelerated policy reloads."
  ],
  "impact": "Transient over-allow for small number of tenants leading to underbilling and potential customer perception issues; visible as short-lived bursts up to ~2x expected throughput for affected keys. Affects hosted and dedicated clusters during rolling updates or instance restarts.",
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "logs_snapshot": [
    "edge: allow decision fastpath: key=K1 shard=sh-23 cache_hit=true priority=high quota_window_id=2026-03-12T10:04:00Z",
    "shard-reassign: lease=renewal failover->sh-27 old_owner=sh-23 new_owner=sh-27",
    "policy-hot-reload: version=v2026-03-12-1 route-fallback=enabled",
    "meter-commit: credits_applied target_bucket=org:T2:key:Kx unexpected=true amount=200"
  ],
  "hypothesis": "A race between sticky-shard mapping update and policy hot-reload causes fast-path cache entries (priority and credit pointers) to be re-keyed incorrectly. Per-key overrides store a pointer to a tenant-scoped credit bucket; during reassignment we are dereferencing a stale pointer and applying credits to the wrong tenant's bucket. Enforcement uses the fast-path decision if cache present, so the wrong credits cause an allow where a deny should occur.",
  "experiment_results": "Replayed the sequence in staging using the shard-reassign harness. With no policy reload the issue did not occur. When timed policy reload coincided with reassignment, we reproduced the over-allow consistently. Enabling stronger pointer validation (temporary patch) eliminated the over-allows in the harness.",
  "root_cause": "Sticky-shard pointer (in-memory bucket reference) is validated only by shard id but not by tenant id during fast-path credit application. Policy hot-reload mutates the route/priority indices while a shard transfer copies pointers; combined these can produce a transient pointer that points at an unrelated tenant's bucket. Enforcement fast-path accepts the cache without full tenant-level validation.",
  "mitigations": "Short-term patch deployed to staging: on fast-path cache hit, perform tenant-id validation on the cached credit pointer before applying credits. Also increased grace period on shard handoff to reduce overlap. Rolled patch to canary edge fleet.",
  "rollout_plan": "1) Canary for 2 hours on low-traffic region with added telemetry (done). 2) Gradual ramp to 30% of traffic with continued trace sampling for next 24 hours. 3) Full rollout after 48 hours if no regressions. 4) Follow with a database reconciliation backfill job to detect credits misapplied in last 7 days and create accounting fixes if needed.",
  "long_term_fix": "Refactor in-memory credit pointer representation to be immutable and namespaced by tenant+shard+route. Replace pointer dereference fast-path with a lightweight validation token check (versioned binder). Add unit and property tests for concurrent shard handoff + policy reload scenarios.",
  "regression_test_plan": "Add deterministic concurrency tests to runtime-policy-simulator: combinations of shard reassignment, policy hot-reload, per-key overrides, and burst credit application. Add e2e test in CI harness that exercises rolling updates with randomized interleavings. Add a smoke check after canary verifying no over-allow traces in last 10 minutes.",
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-430001 (shard-handoff-stabilization)",
    "ENG-429112 (policy-hot-reload-atomicity)",
    "ENG-421007 (prefetch-credit-tombstone-investigation)"
  ],
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood/inference/rateengine-2.0/priority-pointer-design",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/8523 (staging short-term patch)",
    "https://grafana.redwood/board/edge-allow-spikes?from=now-1d&org=tenant",
    "s3://redwood-logs/2026-03-12/shard-hand-off-traces.tar.gz"
  ],
  "notes": [
    "PM (Aisha Kapoor): prioritize mitigation; billing reconciliation may be needed if misapplied credits persist beyond 24h.",
    "Security (Rajiv Patel): no PII involved in pointers but ensure tracing does not expose tenant ids in public dashboards.",
    "Observation: reproduces more reliably when policy reload contains route fallback toggles rather than pure priority edits."
  ],
  "release": "rateengine-2.0.3",
  "security_review_required": "false",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
